claim: UN Fact-Finding Mission reported in August 2019 that MEHL and MEC formed a large military-controlled business network whose revenues materially strengthened the Tatmadaw's institutional capacity.
limitations: Establishes pre-coup economic base; does not prove expenditure on any specific 2021 operation.

claim: Global Witness documented in April 2019 that military-linked companies and armed actors held material interests in the jade economy and that jade revenues were linked to conflict financing in Kachin State.
limitations: Sector and actor relationships differ by location; cannot be generalized to every armed group or post-coup resistance network.

claim: Global Witness's 2015 investigation described official Tatmadaw-linked stakes in the jade sector through MEHL/MEC and reported substantial emporium sales by army companies.
limitations: Historical sector evidence supports structural resource capacity, not a direct causal claim about the 2021 coup.

claim: The 2019 UN economic-interests report identified more than one hundred military businesses owned by MEHL/MEC across mining, manufacturing, banking, insurance and other sectors.
limitations: Corporate network breadth indicates structural capacity; conversion into operational capability requires separate evidence.
